why: Wherever two shapes overlap, the shared part is cut out of BOTH shapes and the pieces move apart. In figure 3 the small triangle and the square both overlap the big triangle, so all those shared parts are cut away: option 1. Option 2 cuts only the square overlap and leaves the small triangle whole; option 4 is figure 3 unchanged.
trick: Look for every overlap in the figure; each one must be removed, not just one.
note: Option drawings are rebuilt geometrically from the question figure; option 3 is an approximate copy of the scan.
